identity.title: ALMACAL II: Extreme Star Formation Rate Densities in Dusty Starbursts Revealed by ALMA 20 mas Resolution Imaging

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present ALMA ultra–high–spatial resolution ($\sim 20 \, {\rm mas}$ or $150 \, {\rm pc}$) observations of dust continuum at $920 \, {\rm \mu m}$ and $1.2 \, {\rm mm}$ in a pair of submm galaxies (SMGs) at $z = 3.442$

targets.name: ALMACAL-1 (A-1) and ALMACAL-2 (A-2) near calibrator J1058+0133

distance_source.value: measured from detected CO and H2O emission lines

question.value: What is the dust morphology and star-formation-rate surface density of a pair of SMGs at z = 3.442 found in the ALMACAL survey, as seen at ~20 mas resolution?

evidence.quote: In this work we present ultra-high-spatial resolution observations ($\sim 20 \, {\rm mas}$) in a pair of submm galaxies (SMGs) at $z = 3.442$ selected from ALMACAL

bands.value: Ultra-high-resolution in B3, B6, B7 (continuum used in B6 and B7); mid-resolution data in several bands (B3-B9)

evidence.quote: There are ultra–high–spatial–resolution observations in B3, B6 and B7. No continuum emission is detected in B3 due to the lack of depth. We thus focus our analysis on B6 and B7.

angular_resolution.value: B7: 25 mas x 18 mas (~920 um); B6: 29 mas x 25 mas; mid-resolution beams >0.3''

evidence.quote: we obtain a beam size of $25 \, {\rm mas} \times 18 \, {\rm mas}$ at $\sim 920 \, {\rm \mu m}$ (B7)
The spatial resolution of the B6 observations is $29 \, {\rm mas} \times 25 \, {\rm mas}$
The continuum sensitivity is $\sigma_{\rm B7} = 30 \, {\rm \mu Jy} \, {\rm beam}^{-1}$.
with a r.m.s. level of $\sigma_{\rm B6} = 40 \, {\rm \mu Jy} \, {\rm beam}^{-1}$

pi_or_archival_as_stated.value: Archival ALMA calibrator data extracted from the ALMA archive

evidence.quote: we also use ultra–high–spatial–resolution data especially extracted from the ALMA archive for the analysis presented in this work

what.value: ALMACAL survey strategy, calibration and source extraction

evidence.quote: The strategy of the survey and the details of data calibration and source extraction can be found in (cite: Oteo2016ApJ...822...36O).

what.value: ALESS average SMG SED template compared with A-1 and A-2

evidence.quote: compares the FIR SED of A–1 and A–2 with the ones for the average population of SMGs in the ALESS survey (cite: Swinbank2014MNRAS.438.1267S) and Arp 220.

self_calibration.value: Self-calibration applied in the ultra-high-resolution data, same as mid-resolution; in-field calibrator

evidence.quote: The extraction and calibration of the ultra-high resolution data is done in exactly the same way as for the mid-resolution data, including self-calibration to improve image quality.
Using Briggs weighting with a `robust` parameter equal to 0.5
We have measured the primary-beam corrected flux density at $920 \, {\rm \mu m}$ and beam–deconvolved size of each component with the task imfit within casa.
we obtain a beam size of $25 \, {\rm mas} \times 18 \, {\rm mas}$ at $\sim 920 \, {\rm \mu m}$ (B7)
The continuum sensitivity is $\sigma_{\rm B7} = 30 \, {\rm \mu Jy} \, {\rm beam}^{-1}$.

what.value: Data extraction, calibration and source extraction of ALMACAL

evidence.quote: The strategy of the survey and the details of data calibration and source extraction can be found in (cite: Oteo2016ApJ...822...36O).

what.value: SFR from L_IR with classical calibration and Salpeter IMF

evidence.quote: The SFR of A–1 and A–2 has been then derived from the total IR luminosity assuming the classical (cite: Kennicutt1998) calibration and a Salpeter IMF
we have used the code `uvmcmcfit`, which models the lensed emission of galaxies observed with interferometers in the $uv$ plane (cite: Bussmann2013ApJ...779...25B; Bussmann2015ApJ...812...43B)

method.value: Archive extraction, calibration and self-calibration as for mid-resolution data; Briggs imaging

evidence.quote: The extraction and calibration of the ultra-high resolution data is done in exactly the same way as for the mid-resolution data, including self-calibration to improve image quality.
Using Briggs weighting with a `robust` parameter equal to 0.5

validation.value: Independent B6 and B7 datasets show the same structure

evidence.quote: we have two independent datasets in ALMA band 6 (B6) and band 7 (B7), which prove the reliability of the structure we see.

analysis_steps.goal: Fit FIR SED for T_dust and L_IR, SFR

method.value: Optically thin dust model plus mid-IR power law fitted to six photometric points (bands split into halves)

evidence.quote: we have fitted their FIR SEDs using optically thin models (with a dust emissivity of $\beta = 2.0$), including a mid-IR power law with a slope of $\alpha = 2.25$.
including a mid-IR power law with a slope of $\alpha = 2.25$

assumptions.value: Total IR luminosity due to star formation; Salpeter IMF; Kennicutt (1998) calibration

evidence.quote: we assume here that the total IR luminosity is due to star formation rather than AGN activity.
the $\chi^2$ of the fits would not be significantly different

validation.value: Compared with ALESS average SMG and Arp 220 templates

evidence.quote: These two templates have been shifted to $z = 3.442$ and scaled to the $460 \, {\rm \mu m}$ flux density of A–1 and A–2.

method.value: imfit on primary-beam corrected 920 um image; only clumps >10 sigma tabulated

evidence.quote: where we only include the three clumps which are detected at $> 10\sigma$, since sizes cannot be reliably measured at lower signal to noise.
the similarity between the B6 and B7 emission in A–1A and A–2A confirm that the dust emission in those two components is truly compact.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive clump L_IR, SFR and SFR surface density

method.value: Rescale best-fit SED to observed clump 920 um flux; Kennicutt SFR; divide by deconvolved area

evidence.quote: The total IR luminosity of each clump has been obtained by re-scaling the best-fit mid-IR power law plus the optically thin dust emission to A–1 and A–2 to their observed $920 \, {\rm \mu m}$ flux density.

assumptions.value: Salpeter IMF; IR luminosity from star formation

evidence.quote: assuming a Salpeter IMF

Such high values of the SFR surface densities have not been reported so far in any high-redshift dust starburst, and exceed the maximum value predicted by (cite: Andrews2011ApJ...727...97A), $\sim 1000 \, {\rm M}_\odot \, {\rm yr}^{-1} \, {\rm kpc}^{-2}$.

method.value: uv-plane lens modelling with elliptical Gaussian source and SIE lens, first on mid-resolution then ultra-high-resolution data

evidence.quote: In `uvmcmcfit` the background source is assumed to have an elliptical Gaussian profile, whereas the lens mass profile is represented by a singular isothermal ellipsoid.

validation.value: Positions and flux ratios well recovered in mid-resolution maps

evidence.quote: The result is that the positions and flux ratios of the two sources are well recovered in all bands.

used_for.value: imfit to measure flux density and deconvolved size

evidence.quote: beam–deconvolved size of each component with the task imfit within casa
we have used the code `uvmcmcfit`, which models the lensed emission of galaxies observed with interferometers in the $uv$ plane
we estimate that we resolve out about 40% of the observed flux in both A–1 and A–2
We have derived $\mu_{\rm dust} = 7.44 +/- 0.04$ at $870 \, {\rm \mu m}$
whose effective radius is only $R_{\rm eff} \sim 40 \, {\rm pc}$
the de-magnified SFR surface density is $\Sigma_{\rm SFR} \sim 10,000 M_\odot \, {\rm yr}^{-1} \, {\rm kpc}^{-2}$

findings_qualitative.value: A-1 resolved into three clumps; A-2 has one; A-1A and A-2A dominate and are compact

evidence.quote: is resolved into three star-forming clumps, A–1A, A–1B, and A–1C

claims.hypothesis: Dusty starbursts contain very compact star-forming regions with extreme SFR surface density
claims.experiment: 20 mas imaging at 920 um and 1.2 mm; clump size and SED-based SFR
claims.finding: Highest SFR surface densities found in high-redshift galaxies

evidence.quote: The star-formation rate (SFR) surface densities of all these clumps are extremely high, $\Sigma_{\rm SFR} \sim 1200$ to $\sim 3000 \, {M_\odot \, {\rm yr}^{-1} \, {\rm kpc}^{-2}}$

claims.hypothesis: The pair is not a lensed system
claims.experiment: Line and SED comparison; lens modelling with uvmcmcfit
claims.result: Different SEDs, CO SLEDs and no Einstein ring; lensing gives R_eff ~40 pc
claims.finding: Lensing is unlikely but would imply Sigma_SFR ~10000

evidence.quote: There is a small probability that A–1 and A–2 are the lensed components of a background source gravitationally amplified by the blazar host.

claims.hypothesis: Long baselines are needed to measure true Sigma_SFR
claims.experiment: Compared size at mid-resolution (B9) with 20 mas data
claims.result: Mid-resolution gives Sigma_SFR ~165, an order of magnitude lower

evidence.quote: This would imply $\Sigma_{\rm SFR} \sim 165 \, M_\odot \, {\rm yr}^{-1} \, {\rm kpc}^{-2}$

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Companions of the calibrator at its redshift, rejected by redshift z=3.442 vs 0.88

evidence.quote: clearly indicates that they are not related to the calibrator (at $z \sim 0.88$)

limitations_admitted.value: AGN contribution to L_IR cannot be assessed, so SFRs may be overestimated

evidence.quote: If there is AGN contribution to the luminosity of the brightest clumps in A–1 and A–2, their SFRs would be overestimated

referee_caveats_inferred: Sigma_SFR depends on single-band flux scaled with an assumed SED
Size uncertainties from imfit at modest S/N
About 40% of flux resolved out, so clump fraction is uncertain
